title: Heaps & Priority Queues
subtitle: A heap exposes the best current candidate without sorting every candidate, so the invariant is about the root rather than the whole array.
variables: n = input items, k = selection size/rank, u = distinct keys, r = input streams/lists, N = total merged items, V/E = vertices/edges, H = physical heap entries including stale records, a = live tasks, T = produced schedule length, B = payload/key size when relevant. Standard-library heapq is a min-heap on a list; max-heaps here use negative numeric keys for Python 3.10 compatibility. Comparisons/arithmetic use a fixed-word model; Python big integers cost by bit length. Hash operations are expected O(1), with O(B) initial hashing/comparison costs for long keys. Heap push/pop comparison work is logarithmic; Python list capacity growth/shrink makes allocation bounds amortized across operations (a resize may copy O(n) references). Auxiliary space excludes output unless stated; stale heap entries and sorted copies are included. Keys must be consistently ordered, with no NaN. Ties require explicit counters when payloads are unorderable. For offline query sweeps m = queries. Current Python documentation also has max-heap APIs (added in Python 3.14); negated numeric priorities intentionally support Python 3.10+.

Schedule available maximum, or emit idle gap until next release.
patternDetails.related: Compare Greedy rearrangement by what the heap root certifies and what makes entries eligible.
patternDetails.variations: Count-only answer is max(n,(fmax-1)*(cooldown+1)+number_of_max_tasks), avoiding huge idle output.

steps: Pop most frequent available symbol.
Withhold previous symbol until successor chosen.
Reinsert remaining previous count; fail if leftover cannot be placed.
patternDetails.related: Compare Smallest covering range by what the heap root certifies and what makes entries eligible.
patternDetails.variations: Distance>1 becomes cooldown scheduling; arbitrary unequal spacing needs new reasoning.

steps: Seed one item from every list and track maximum.
Evaluate [heap minimum,maximum].
Advance minimum list; stop when any list is exhausted.
patternDetails.related: Compare Best-first Cartesian pairs by what the heap root certifies and what makes entries eligible.
patternDetails.variations: One empty list makes coverage impossible; tie-break equal widths by smaller lower endpoint.

steps: Seed one frontier for each relevant sorted row.
Pop globally smallest pair sum.
Advance only that row column and stop after k outputs/exhaustion.
templates: K smallest pair sums from sorted arrays
patternDetails.related: Compare Lazy keyed priority updates by what the heap root certifies and what makes entries eligible.
patternDetails.variations: Unsorted arrays must be sorted first with original-index tracking if requested.

steps: Create unique version per set and map live key to it.
Skip popped records not identical to live version.
Compact when physical entries exceed threshold relative to live size.
templates: Versioned mutable priority queue with compaction
patternDetails.related: Compare Optimal merge / Huffman by what the heap root certifies and what makes entries eligible.
patternDetails.variations: Indexed heaps can offer different latency bounds; threshold rebuilds and stale drains make this implementation amortized.

steps: Validate nonnegative weights and heapify a copy.
Pop two minimum weights and charge their sum.
Reinsert combined weight until at most one remains.
patternDetails.related: Compare Sweep-line selected candidates by what the heap root certifies and what makes entries eligible.
patternDetails.variations: Huffman coding stores children at each merge, while cost-only template returns the weight sum.

steps: Sort intervals by start and queries with original indices.
Add candidates whose starts <= query.
Pop expired roots and answer shortest live root; restore original query order.
patternDetails.related: Compare Max-capital eligibility by what the heap root certifies and what makes entries eligible.
patternDetails.variations: Expired interior entries can remain safely until they reach root; total pushes/pops bounded by n.

steps: Sort projects by capital threshold.
Push profits of every newly affordable project.
Choose largest positive profit, increase capital, repeat at most k times.
patternDetails.related: Compare Bounded Top-K by what the heap root certifies and what makes entries eligible.
patternDetails.variations: Negative profits are skipped for at-most-k; exactly-k or dependencies invalidate that stopping rule.

decisionProcess: 0–30s: identify requested extremum/rank, static versus online, comparable key/tie policy, updates/deletions and whether full sorting is needed.
30–60s: retain largest k -> min-heap of winners; online median -> two heaps; merge sorted sources -> one head per source. Heap direction exposes worst winner or best available as required.
60–90s: nonnegative weighted shortest paths -> Dijkstra; unit weights -> BFS;0/1 -> deque. Validate weights and stale-state rule.
90–120s: intervals/projects -> sort eligibility then heap the choice key; cooldown -> available heap plus release queue; optimal merge -> two smallest with exchange proof.

120–180s: write invariant and prove greedy choice where applicable. Account for sorting copies, output length, stale H, compaction latency, key comparisons and Python list resizing. Test ties, empty, k bounds and stale root.

templateDetails.preconditions: Finite comparable numbers, integer k. Returns exactly k values in descending order including duplicates; no mutation. Invalid k raises ValueError.
templateDetails.observation: Sorted output adds O(k log k), included in total.

templateDetails.preconditions: Positive integer k, comparable numeric stream without NaN. add returns kth largest including duplicates, or None until k arrivals; does not retain the whole stream. Initialization O(m log(k+1)).
templateDetails.observation: Smallest retained winner is kth largest.

templateDetails.preconditions: Sequence/iterable of strings; output k distinct words by descending frequency then ascending lexicographic order. k=0 returns []; invalid k raises ValueError. No mutation; long-string hashing/comparison adds cost.
templateDetails.observation: Equal-count lexical worst must be root for eviction.

templateDetails.preconditions: Each finite stream is sorted nondecreasing with mutually comparable values. Returns merged value list. Consumes iterators, does not mutate source lists. Equal-value interstream order is insertion-serial order, not guaranteed source-index stability.
templateDetails.observation: Only next item per sorted stream is eligible.

templateDetails.preconditions: Sorted nondecreasing acyclic singly linked lists whose nodes are pairwise disjoint. Returns merged head, None if all empty. Mutates/reuses next links; original separate list topology is consumed. Unique serial avoids Node comparison on ties.
templateDetails.observation: Counter avoids Node comparisons; disjointness prevents shared-link corruption.

templateDetails.preconditions: Accepts Python ints, bool rejected. Returns int for odd count and exact Fraction for even count, avoiding float precision/overflow. Convert with float only when approximate judge/API output is desired. Big-integer/Fraction arithmetic is not unit-cost.
templateDetails.observation: Order and size balance are both necessary.

templateDetails.preconditions: Directed mapping to reusable lists of (hashable neighbor, finite nonnegative int/float weight). Missing vertex key is a sink. Returns reachable distances only; absent source gives {source:0}; no mutation. Counter supports unorderable vertices. For floats, accumulated distances must remain representable and comparisons are subject to rounding.

Finite numeric (start,end) intervals interpreted as [start,end). Zero-length intervals ignored; invalid reversed endpoints raise ValueError. Returns peak active count; [] -> 0. Sorts a copy, no input mutation.
templateDetails.observation: Touching half-open intervals can reuse a room.

templateDetails.preconditions: Hashable unit-duration tasks except None; nonnegative integer uniform cooldown. Returns a minimum-length schedule with None idle slots, each input task occurrence used once. Does not mutate input; may allocate a large output when cooldown is huge. Idle gaps use repeat rather than allocating a second gap-sized temporary list, keeping auxiliary state O(u) apart from the returned schedule.
templateDetails.observation: Uniform cooldown release times are FIFO.

templateDetails.preconditions: String input, character identity uses Python code points (not grapheme clusters). Returns any anagram with no adjacent equal chars, or empty string if impossible/empty. Does not mutate input.
templateDetails.observation: Withhold previous symbol to forbid adjacent repetition.

templateDetails.preconditions: Nonempty sorted nondecreasing integer lists. Returns inclusive (low,high) covering at least one element per list; minimizes width then low. No lists or any empty list -> None. No mutation; sortedness is a caller precondition.
templateDetails.observation: Advance only minimum head while tracking maximum.

templateDetails.preconditions: Sorted nondecreasing integer sequences; nonnegative integer k. Returns up to k value pairs in nondecreasing sum order, ties by source indices. Equal values at distinct indices remain distinct choices. No mutation.
templateDetails.observation: Sorted rows need one candidate each.

templateDetails.preconditions: Hashable stable keys; consistently comparable finite numeric priorities; arbitrary unorderable payloads. set inserts/replaces key, equal priorities execute oldest-current-set first (FIFO by latest set timestamp; replacing a key moves it behind already-live ties); remove returns bool; pop returns (key,priority,payload), raises IndexError when no live items. New versions invalidate old entries by identity. With compaction H <= 2a+16 after edits, a single pop can drain O(a+1) stale entries at O(log(a+2)) each: O((a+1) log(a+2)) worst case. A threshold rebuild costs O(a+1), while set can cost O(a+1) on a rebuild and remove likewise. Amortized O(log(a+2)) bounds charge each stale extraction to the edit that created it and each rebuild to the many invalidations since the preceding rebuild; use the maximum live size across a sequence for a uniform sequence bound.
templateDetails.observation: Current entry identity is authoritative; stale entries still use memory.

templateDetails.preconditions: Finite nonnegative int/float weights, representable accumulated sums. Returns minimum sum of pair-combine costs; zero or one input -> 0. Copies input, consumes iterables; float rounding applies. Huffman construction additionally stores child references.
templateDetails.observation: Two smallest can be deepest siblings in an optimal merge.

templateDetails.preconditions: Closed integer intervals [left,right], integer query sequence. Returns shortest inclusive length per original query position, -1 if uncovered. No mutation; duplicates allowed. Expired non-root records can stay until they affect minimum; n intervals, m queries.
templateDetails.observation: Only roots require pruning before a minimum query.

templateDetails.preconditions: Finite integer capital/requirements/profits; projects independent, requirement is a threshold not a spent cost. Choose at most k distinct projects; negative profits can be skipped. Returns greatest final capital; no mutation. Greedy fails with hidden dependencies or spending capital.
templateDetails.observation: Best affordable positive profit leaves no less capital.

practiceDetails.insight: Negate largest priority, reinsert positive difference.
Bounded min-heap. Duplicates count toward rank.
Boundary selection avoids full sort; quickselect offers expected linear alternative.
Count before selecting among unique keys.
Squared distance avoids sqrt; evict worst retained distance.
Equal frequencies need lexical output and reversed eviction tie.
One head per sorted disjoint input.
Two heaps. Partition and size invariants.
End<=start frees half-open room.
Construct with heap+release queue or use length-only formula.
Withhold previous symbol until successor chosen.
Sorted row merge. Repeated values represent distinct index pairs.
Advance only min-list while tracking current maximum.
Fresh minimum finalizes only with nonnegative weights.
Two smallest can be optimal deepest siblings.
Threshold is eligibility, not spent cost; choose best positive profit.
Sorted queries make candidate arrivals monotone.
Insertion-only median needs delayed deletes, valid sizes and stale-root pruning for windows.
One recent cursor per user yields k-way descending merge.
Authoritative task version invalidates old heap entries.
